HACS_PURPOSE_TEXT_1: Your device is 100% standalone and works perfectly on its own. However, if you have a Home Assistant server, this optional integration allows you to create a seamless gateway to take the experience even further.
HACS_PURPOSE_TEXT_2: It automatically imports all your devices (shutters, blinds, gates, etc.) as standard cover entities. You can track their exact position in real time (even when controlled by a physical remote), operate them via voice control, and include them in your automations (weather, leaving home, or any other scenario...).

PAIR_SHADE_DESC: Configuration wizard to guide you step-by-step through pairing your device with ESPSomfy-RTS.
PAIR_SHADE_STEP_1_1: Open the device's memory using a remote already paired with the motor: press the Prog button (usually on the back) until the device jogs briefly.
PAIR_SHADE_STEP_2_1: Now press the PROG button above to send the pairing signal to your equipment.
PAIR_SHADE_STEP_3_1: If your device correctly performed the second back-and-forth movement in the previous step, click Save to finish adding it to your system.
UNPAIR_SHADE_DESC: Configuration wizard to guide you step-by-step through unpairing your device from ESPSomfy-RTS.
UNPAIR_SHADE_STEP_1_1: Open the device's memory using an existing remote: press the Prog button (usually on the back) until the device jogs briefly.
UNPAIR_SHADE_STEP_2_1: Now press the PROG button above to send the unpairing signal to your equipment.
UNPAIR_SHADE_STEP_3_1: If your device correctly performed the second back-and-forth movement in the previous step, click Save to finish removing it from your system.
PAIR_GARAGE_DESC: Configuration wizard to guide you step-by-step through pairing your garage door with ESPSomfy-RTS.
PAIR_GARAGE_STEP_3_1: If your device correctly performed the second back-and-forth movement in the previous step, click Save to finish adding it to your system.
UNPAIR_GARAGE_DESC: Configuration wizard to guide you step-by-step through unpairing your garage door from ESPSomfy-RTS.
UNPAIR_GARAGE_STEP_3_1: If your device correctly performed the second back-and-forth movement in the previous step, click Save to finish removing it from your system.
WIZ_SHADE_STEP_1_2: Programming mode is now active for 2 minutes. You have plenty of time to continue calmly. Press the NEXT button.
WIZ_SHADE_STEP_1_3: While 2 minutes is the RTS standard, feel free to check your model's manual if the motor seems to exit programming mode faster.
WIZ_SHADE_STEP_2_2: It should jog again to confirm the registration. On some models, a long press may be necessary.
WIZ_SHADE_STEP_2_3: If the movement occurred, congratulations! Your device is ready. You can proceed to the final step by pressing the NEXT button.
WIZ_SHADE_STEP_2_4: If nothing happened, don't panic: the memory might still be open. Try pressing the PROG button above again.
WIZ_GARAGE_STEP_1_1: Open your garage motor's memory (Refer to your manual to identify the exact procedure).
WIZ_GARAGE_STEP_1_2: Once the memory is open, don't rush; you usually have 2 minutes to act (please check your specific manual).
WIZ_GARAGE_STEP_1_3: You can now proceed to the next step by pressing the NEXT button.
WIZ_GARAGE_STEP_2_1: Press the PROG button above. ESPSomfy-RTS will send a Toggle command for single-button remotes, or a Prog signal for 3-button models.
WIZ_GARAGE_STEP_2_2: You can now press the NEXT button.
LINK_GROUP_DESC: Setup wizard to guide you step-by-step through adding your device to the group
LINK_GROUP_TITLE_STEP2: Selection of the device to be paired
LINK_GROUP_TITLE_STEP4: Pairing your device to the group
LINK_GROUP_STEP_1_1: This wizard will guide you through adding device to this group. Please follow each instruction carefully until the process is complete.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_1_2: During this procedure, the device must perform exactly two jog movements (brief up-and-down): the first to open the motor memory and the second to confirm the group addition.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_1_3: Each piece of device must be paired individually. When you are ready to begin, press the NEXT button.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_2_1: Choose the device you wish to include in this group using the selector above.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_2_2: Once the device is selected, press the NEXT button to continue.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_2_3: Only device not yet associated with this group is displayed. Note that a single device can belong to several different groups.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_3_1: Press the OPEN MEMORY button above. The selected device should perform a brief jog to confirm its memory is open.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_3_2: If the movement occurred, click YES in the confirmation window to proceed to the final step. Otherwise, click NO and try opening the memory again.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_3_3: The motor should only perform one jog. If it performs several, the memory has been closed by mistake. A confirmation window will appear following your action.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_4_1: Press the PAIR TO GROUP button above to send the final association command.
LINK_GROUP_STEP_4_2: A confirmation window will appear. If the motor performed another jog, click YES. The wizard will then close automatically, and the association will be complete.
LINK_GROUP_MEMORY_READY_FOR_GROUP: Once the device jogs, the motor memory will be ready to add the device to the group.
LINK_GROUP_LINK_DONE: Once the device jogs, it will be added to the group and the process will be complete.
UNLINK_GROUP_DESC: Setup wizard to guide you step-by-step through removing your device from the group
UNLINK_GROUP_TITLE_STEP_3: Unpairing your device from the group
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_1_1: This wizard will guide you through removing this device from the group. Follow all instructions at each step until the device is removed from the group.
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_1_2: During this process, the device must perform exactly two jog movements. The first indicates the motor memory is open, and the second confirms the group has been deleted from the motor memory.
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_1_3: Each piece of device must be removed from the group individually. When you are ready to begin dissociating the device from the group, press the NEXT button to start.
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_2_1: You must first open the device's memory by pressing the OPEN MEMORY button. The device should perform a jog to indicate the memory is open.
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_2_2: If the movement occurred, click YES in the confirmation window to proceed to the final step. Otherwise, click NO and try opening the memory again.
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_2_3: The motor should only perform one jog. If it performs more than one, it means the motor memory has been closed.
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_3_1: Now you must send the group dissociation command; press the UNPAIR FROM GROUP button above.
UNLINK_GROUP_STEP_3_2: A confirmation window will appear. If the motor performed another jog, click YES. The wizard will then close automatically, and the dissociation will be complete.
UNLINK_GROUP_METHOD_1: If you have trouble getting the motor to react at this stage, you can try opening the memory using a remote control. This is usually done by selecting the channel and then holding the PROG button down.
UNLINK_GROUP_METHOD_2: If you have opened the memory using this alternative method, press the NO button to close this message, then the NEXT button to skip this step.

CAL_DESC: Automatically times this device's up, down and tilt travel by actually moving it, and detects the tilt/lift order for integrated tilt motors.
CAL_INTRO_TEXT: At each step, click Start right before the device begins moving, then Stop as soon as it has finished: timing happens automatically while you watch it. The device will actually move during this procedure.
CAL_BLIND_Q_TITLE: What kind of tilt does this device have?
CAL_BLIND_OPT_NONE_DESC: This device does not tilt its slats -- only its travel (open/close) will be measured.
CAL_BLIND_OPT_TILTMOTOR_DESC: A second motor tilts the slats independently of travel. Travel and tilt will be measured separately.
CAL_BLIND_OPT_INTEGRATED_DESC: The same motor tilts the slats then moves the device (or the reverse) -- the wizard will also ask which happens first.
CAL_BLIND_OPT_TILTONLY_DESC: This device has no travel -- only the slat tilt will be measured.
CAL_BLIND_OPT_EUROMODE_DESC: Travel and tilt handled together by the same motor, with no order ambiguity to detect.
CAL_UP_INSTRUCTION: The device must be fully closed before starting. Click Start, then Stop as soon as it is fully open.
CAL_DOWN_INSTRUCTION: The device must be fully open before starting. Click Start, then Stop as soon as it is fully closed.
CAL_TILT_UP_INSTRUCTION: The slats must be fully closed before starting. Click Start, then Stop as soon as the slats are flat.
CAL_TILT_UP_INSTRUCTION_INTEGRATED: The slats must be fully closed before starting. Click Start, then Stop as soon as the slats stop moving and the device starts to travel -- that is the end of the tilt phase.
CAL_TILT_DOWN_INSTRUCTION: The slats must be fully flat before starting. Click Start, then Stop as soon as the slats are fully closed.
CAL_TILT_DOWN_INSTRUCTION_INTEGRATED: The slats must be fully flat before starting. Click Start, then Stop as soon as the slats stop moving and the device starts to travel -- that is the end of the tilt phase.
CAL_ORDER_INTRO: Some integrated tilt motors tilt the slats before moving the device, others do the opposite depending on direction. Test each direction and watch what happens first.
CAL_ORDER_QUESTION_OPEN_DESC: On if the slats tilt before the device starts opening
CAL_ORDER_QUESTION_CLOSE_DESC: On if the slats tilt before the device starts closing
CAL_SUMMARY_TEXT: Review the measured values before saving. Times that were not measured keep their current value.
CAL_SUMMARY_EMPTY: No measurement taken -- current values will be kept.
CAL_ERR_SAVE: Could not save the measured values. Please try again.
CAL_ERR_DURATION_TOO_SHORT: Too short for a real movement -- measurement ignored, try again.
CAL_ERR_DURATION_TOO_LONG: Too long (> 180 s) -- measurement ignored, try again.
CAL_ADJUST_INTRO: Measured time doesn't quite match the real movement?
CAL_ADJUST_TOO_EARLY_DESC: Stop was clicked before the movement actually finished -- adds 0.1 s.
CAL_ADJUST_TOO_LATE_DESC: Stop was clicked after the movement had already finished -- removes 0.1 s.
ROLLING_CODE_DESC: Warning: an incorrect value may break communication with the shade
ROLLING_CODE_WARNING_DESC_1: If this device is already paired with a motor, changing the rolling code will cause it to malfunction. Rolling codes are linked to the remote address, and the motor expects them to be sequential.
ROLLING_CODE_WARNING_DESC_2: If you hesitate even slightly, do not press the red button. Green represents safety — press it, wipe the sweat from your forehead, and follow the normal pairing process.

REPEAT_REMOTE_DESC_2: Once assigned, ESPSomfy-RTS will act as a repeater and repeat all signals from the identified remote controls.
REPEAT_REMOTE_DESC_3: Assign a repeater only when ESPSomfy-RTS reliably receives a physical remote control but the motor does not.
REPEAT_REMOTE_DESC_4: Repeating unnecessary radio signals will degrade radio performance, and never assign the same repeater to more than one ESPSomfy-RTS device. You would create an insidious echo chamber.

RADIO_DESC: Activation, configuration, and adjustment of your radio settings
RADIO_TOOLTIP_GPIO_1: The name (e.g., SCLK) refers to the pin on the CC1101 module.
RADIO_TOOLTIP_GPIO_2: The GPIO number (e.g., GPIO18) refers to the physical pin on your ESP32.
RADIO_TOOLTIP_GPIO_3: Refer to the 'pinout' diagram of your specific ESP32 model to locate them.
RADIO_SAFETY_TEXT: I understand the risks of misconfiguring the GPIOs.
RADIO_TUNER_EXPLAIN: ESPSomfy-RTS receives everything that falls within this band, and transmits on the base frequency.
RADIO_TUNER_ALT: Reception window from {min} to {max} MHz, {bande} kHz wide.
RADIO_SCAN_HINT_TITLE: Your devices not responding, or responding poorly?
RADIO_SCAN_HINT_DESC: The scan listens across the whole 433 MHz band and pinpoints the frequency your remotes actually transmit on.
RADIO_TEST_DESC: ESPSomfy-RTS must recognise the signal from your remotes in order to drive your devices. This test checks that it does.
RADIO_TEST_WAITING: Press a button on your remote
RADIO_TEST_WAITING_DESC: Any button, within range of the device. A short press is enough.
RADIO_TEST_NONE_DESC: This does not mean your settings are wrong. First check that you actually pressed a button, that the battery is not flat, and that you are within range. If the test still fails, the wizard can find the right setting.
RADIO_TEST_WIZ_DESC: If the problem persists, the wizard listens to your remotes one by one, measures the frequency they actually transmit on, and sets ESPSomfy-RTS to it.
RADIO_TEST_OK_DESC: “{command}” command received at {rssi}. There is nothing to adjust here.
RADIO_TEST_OK_HINT: Several remotes? Test them one at a time.
RADIO_RECAP_DESC: Read-only — the wizard can adjust these values for you.
RADIO_RECAP_NOTE: These three settings decide which frequency ESPSomfy-RTS listens on for your remotes, how much tolerance it allows around that frequency, and how much power it uses to command your devices. The default values suit most installations.
RADIO_RECAP_PENDING_ROW: Not saved — the board is running {v}
RADIO_OFF_MSG: Enable the radio at the top of this page, then save: without it, ESPSomfy-RTS hears nothing and this test cannot succeed.
RADIO_OFF_UNSAVED: You have enabled the radio but the change has not been saved yet. Click Save, then try again.
RADIO_WIZ_DESC: Useful if your equipment does not respond, or if only some of it obeys: that is a sign your remotes do not all transmit on the same frequency. The wizard measures them and finds the setting that covers them all.
RADIO_WIZ_STEP1_DESC: They will be measured one at a time. Stand about one metre from ESPSomfy-RTS — no further, and not pressed against it.
RADIO_WIZ_PRESS_DESC: Hold down any button, about one metre from the device. A remote stops transmitting by itself after about ten seconds: if nothing appears, release and press again. Two or three presses are normal.
RADIO_WIZ_MEASURED_DESC: It transmits on {freq} MHz, received at {rssi} dBm. Do you have another remote to measure?
RADIO_WIZ_SILENT_DESC: Nothing was picked up. Check that you are holding a button down, that the battery is not flat, and that you are about one metre from the device.
RADIO_WIZ_PARTIAL_DESC: A signal was picked up, but too briefly to be measured. Press again and hold the button until the measurement appears.
RADIO_WIZ_OUTLIER_TITLE: One measurement does not match the others
RADIO_WIZ_OUTLIER_DESC: Remote {n}, measured at {freq} MHz, is far from the others — {ecart} kHz apart in total. It is probably another device picked up by mistake. Keeping it would mean widening the bandwidth so much that reception of all the others would suffer.
RADIO_WIZ_RESULT_STOCK: Your remotes are closely grouped: the factory bandwidth suits them. Only the frequency has been aligned to them.
RADIO_WIZ_RESULT_WIDENED: Your remotes do not all transmit on the same frequency. The bandwidth has been widened just enough to cover them all.
RADIO_HELP_BASE_FREQUENCY: This is the frequency your radio module, your motors and your Somfy remotes communicate on. Just like a radio station, transmitter and receiver must be tuned to the same frequency. The factory value (433.42 MHz) suits almost every installation. Only change it in very small steps if you have serious reception problems (short range, missed commands). When in doubt, go back to the default value.
RADIO_HELP_RX_BANDWIDTH: This sets the width of the receiver's listening “window”. A narrow window rejects interference better and improves range, but demands a precise frequency setting. A wide window makes it easier to pick up slightly off-frequency remotes, but also picks up more ambient noise. Keep the original value, and only widen it if you struggle to pick up your remotes.
RADIO_HELP_TX_POWER: This is how strongly commands are transmitted (in dBm). The default value (10 dBm) is more than enough to cover a house. Higher power theoretically increases range, but can cause interference. Only go to 12 dBm if your hardware is explicitly designed for it, at the risk of malfunction or a shorter lifespan.
